ai.description: This 30–40 mm frog has a mottled brown or olive back with dark spots. It features a pointed snout, a distinct white mid-dorsal stripe, and a pale, granular belly. It lacks a vocal sac.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Euphlyctis karaavali* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, bright yellow or orange patch on its groin and the hidden surfaces of its thighs.
ai.habitat: *Euphlyctis karaavali* inhabits low-altitude coastal plains and wetlands, typically found in paddy fields and freshwater marshes within the humid Western Ghats region.
ai.behavior: The Karaavali Skittering Frog is primarily nocturnal and exhibits a unique defensive strategy by rapidly skittering across water surfaces to evade potential predators.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Euphlyctis karaavali* is an oviparous breeder that lays eggs in seasonal ponds. It breeds during the monsoon season, typically producing clutches of several hundred eggs.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Euphlyctis karaavali* is endemic to the coastal plains of Karnataka and Kerala in southwestern India, typically occurring at low elevations below 200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The *Euphlyctis karaavali* produces a series of rapid, high-pitched "tink-tink" pulses, typically heard while the frog is submerged in shallow, stagnant freshwater habitats.
